title: A bounded-above finite-free model of a module complex glues from a finite standard-open cover
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $M^\bullet$ be a complex of $A$-modules. Let $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$ generate the unit ideal, and write $M^\bullet_{f_i}=M^\bullet\otimes_A A_{f_i}$. View complexes as objects of the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Call an object $C$ of $D(A)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $A$-modules and a morphism $E^\bullet\to C$ in $D(A)$ inducing isomorphisms $H^j(E^\bullet)\to H^j(C)$ for $j>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C)$. Call $C$ pseudo-coherent if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules. If every $M^\bullet_{f_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $M^\bullet$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. If every $M^\bullet_{f_i}$ is pseudo-coherent, then $M^\bullet$ is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.4 (Tag 066D, more-algebra-lemma-glue-pseudo-coherent), pseudo-coherent clause, read through Lemma 064Z (more-algebra-lemma-pseudo-coherent)

proof.text: Fix an integer $m$. We prove the $m$-pseudo-coherent clause in the form: every complex $K^\bullet$ of $A$-modules whose localizations $K^\bullet_{f_i}=K^\bullet\otimes_AA_{f_i}$ are $m$-pseudo-coherent (over $A_{f_i}$) is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Localization is exact, so $H^j(K^\bullet)_{f_i}=H^j(K^\bullet_{f_i})$. Each $K^\bullet_{f_i}$ receives a morphism from a bounded complex inducing isomorphisms on $H^j$ for $j>m$, so $H^j(K^\bullet_{f_i})=0$ for $j$ large; let $n$ be the largest integer with $H^n(K^\bullet_{f_i})\neq0$ for some $i$ ($n=-\infty$ if there is none). Since the $f_i$ generate the unit ideal, a module whose localizations at all $f_i$ vanish is zero, so $H^j(K^\bullet)=0$ for $j>n$. We induct on $n-m$. If $n<m$, then $H^j(K^\bullet)=0$ for every $j\ge m$, and $K^\bullet$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent by [lem-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent-vanishing-base].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.4 (Tag 066D), proof: setup and the case $n<m$ via Tag 064W

proof.text: Let $n\ge m$. The morphism witnessing that $K^\bullet_{f_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent also witnesses that it is $n$-pseudo-coherent (isomorphisms on $H^j$ for $j>n$, and on $H^n$ an isomorphism if $n>m$, a surjection if $n=m$), and $H^j(K^\bullet_{f_i})=0$ for $j>n$. Hence [lem-sc-finite-cohomology], applied over $A_{f_i}$ with the integer $n$, shows that $H^n(K^\bullet)_{f_i}=H^n(K^\bullet_{f_i})$ is a finite $A_{f_i}$-module for each $i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-of-localization-span] shows that $H^n(K^\bullet)$ is a finite $A$-module. Choose a finite free $A$-module $E$ and a surjection $E\to H^n(K^\bullet)$; since $E$ is free it lifts to $E\to\operatorname{Ker}(d^n_K)$, giving a map of complexes $\alpha\colon E[-n]\to K^\bullet$ that is surjective on $H^n$. Let $C(\alpha)^\bullet$ be its cone, so $E[-n]\to K^\bullet\to C(\alpha)^\bullet\to E[-n][1]$ is a distinguished triangle in $D(A)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.4 (Tag 066D), proof: finiteness of $H^n$ via Tag 064S and Algebra, Lemma 00EO, and the choice of $\alpha$

proof.text: The long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle, with $H^j(E[-n])=0$ for $j\neq n$, $H^n(E[-n])=E\to H^n(K^\bullet)$ surjective and $H^j(K^\bullet)=0$ for $j>n$, gives $H^j(C(\alpha)^\bullet)=0$ for $j\ge n$. Localization is exact and commutes with shifts and cones, so $E[-n]_{f_i}\to K^\bullet_{f_i}\to C(\alpha)^\bullet_{f_i}\to E[-n]_{f_i}[1]$ is a distinguished triangle in $D(A_{f_i})$, and $H^j(C(\alpha)^\bullet_{f_i})=0$ for $j\ge n$. The complex $E[-n]_{f_i}$ is a bounded complex of finite free $A_{f_i}$-modules, so the identity shows it is $k$-pseudo-coherent for every $k$, in particular $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent. The first clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle] over $A_{f_i}$ shows that each $C(\alpha)^\bullet_{f_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. For $C(\alpha)^\bullet$ the largest degree of nonzero local cohomology is $<n$, so the induction hypothesis shows that $C(\alpha)^\bullet$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. As $E[-n]$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, the second clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle] over $A$, applied to $E[-n]\to K^\bullet\to C(\alpha)^\bullet\to E[-n][1]$, shows that $K^\bullet$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Taking $K^\bullet=M^\bullet$ proves the first assertion.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.4 (Tag 066D), proof: cone induction via Tag 064R

proof.text: For the pseudo-coherent clause, assume every $M^\bullet_{f_i}$ is pseudo-coherent over $A_{f_i}$. By the implication from pseudo-coherence to $m$-pseudo-coherence for every $m$ in [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m] over $A_{f_i}$, each $M^\bullet_{f_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$. By the first assertion, proved in the previous steps for an arbitrary $m$, $M^\bullet$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$. By the converse implication of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m] over $A$, $M^\bullet$ is pseudo-coherent, that is, quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules.

lean.statement: theorem ringPseudoCoherent_localization_glue {A : Type u₁} [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v₁} A)] (m : ℤ) (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v₁} A) ℤ) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) [∀ i : Fin r, HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v₁} (Localization.Away (f i)))] (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) : ((∀ i : Fin r, IsMPseudoCoherent m (Q.obj ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f i)))) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M))) → IsMPseudoCoherent m (Q.obj M)) ∧ ((∀ i : Fin r, IsPseudoCoherent (Q.obj ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f i)))) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M))) → IsPseudoCoherent (Q.obj M))
